Plot covariate balance for two-period implicit weights

Source: R/two_period_covs.R
ggtwfeweights.two_period_covs_obj.Rd

Plots the difference in covariate means between the treated and untreated groups before and after applying the implicit weights from two_period_reg_weights() or two_period_aipw_weights().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'two_period_covs_obj'
ggtwfeweights(
  x,
  plot_outcome = FALSE,
  plot_relative_to_target = FALSE,
  absolute_value = TRUE,
  standardize = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A two_period_covs_obj object.

plot_outcome

Whether to include the change in the outcome in the plot. Default FALSE.

plot_relative_to_target

If TRUE, plot the weighted treated group, the weighted untreated group and the unweighted untreated group relative to the (unweighted) treated group, which shows whether the weights move the treated group away from its own covariate distribution. This adds an extra point per covariate. Default FALSE.

absolute_value

Whether to plot the absolute value of the differences. Default TRUE.

standardize

Whether to divide the differences by the pooled standard deviation of each covariate (pooled_sd()). Default TRUE.

...

Not used.

Value

A ggplot object.

Examples

data(castle, package = "causaldata")
castle <- as.data.frame(castle)
castle2 <- subset(castle, year %in% c(2000, 2010))
castle2$G <- BMisc::get_group(castle2, "sid", tname = "year", treatname = "post")
tw <- two_period_reg_weights(
  yname = "l_homicide", tname = "year", idname = "sid", gname = "G",
  xformula = ~ l_police + unemployrt, data = castle2
)
